name: Inzatsu 131
parentage: Assamica varietal x a native Shizuoka Zairai
description: An old and unique Japanese cultivar that is a hybrid of an Assamica variety and a native Zairai. It is known for its exotic, almost foreign aroma that is highly floral and sometimes spicy, reminiscent of teas from Darjeeling or Taiwan. It is a rare cultivar, prized by connoisseurs for its unique character.
environment: Well-suited to the climate of Shizuoka where it was developed.
processing: Processing Inzatsu 131 aims to highlight its unique, non-Japanese aroma. The method can be adapted to push it towards a greener or a more oxidized style depending on the tea maker's goal.
oxidation: Oxidation can vary. As a Sencha, it is unoxidized. However, it is often allowed a slight oxidation (like an oolong) to further develop its exotic floral and spicy notes.
roasting: Roasting is typically light to preserve its unique aroma.
versatility: Highly versatile. Its unique hybrid genetics make it a rare cultivar that can be successfully crafted into a wide range of styles, from a unique green tea to a fragrant oolong or black tea.

Sencha.Exotic Sencha: When made as a green tea, it has a powerful, exotic floral aroma unlike any other Sencha.

Japanese Black/Oolong.Aromatic Teas: Its Assamica lineage makes it an excellent candidate for producing highly aromatic, lightly oxidized oolongs or even full black teas.

sensory.aroma: Exotic flowers, spicy, muscatel, sometimes a hint of citrus
sensory.flavor: Aromatic, slightly spicy, with a unique floral sweetness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and medium-bodied with a very fragrant and lasting finish. The liquor is often a deeper golden-yellow.
